issues.failure_explanation: The space {v in C(X) : v|_{T_l} in P_k, P_k polynomials of degree up to k in each variable} enforces global continuity, so its dimension equals the number of global (shared) nodes, which is strictly less than L*k^d, and each cell carries (k+1)^d local degrees of freedom, not k^d. Counterexample: d=1, k=1, L cells gives continuous piecewise linears of dimension L+1, not L. Consequently the claimed nodal basis built from k^d nodes per cell with psi_i(a_j)=delta_ij cannot span the stated space.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the count to the standard finite-element dimension (per-cell (k+1)^d degrees of freedom, with dofs on shared faces identified), i.e. N = Theta(L(k+1)^d) = O((k/h)^d) up to boundary terms, and adjust the node construction; purely local edit to the example.
issues.overall_effect: The example's advertised dimension formula and node-count construction are false; the qualitative message (N = O((k/h)^d), many empty cells for small M) survives, and no labelled theorem relies on the exact count.
issues.title: False dimension count for the continuous finite element space in Example FEM example
issues.why_classification: A local correction of a counting formula in an illustrative example; no theorem, rate, or advertised guarantee depends on the exact count.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and $\Aa\colon\Dd\to\Ff$ is a continuous operator with $\norm{\Aa}\leq 1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds the error by eps*||f||_D + C*eps*||A||*||f|| and then claims this is <= ||A||*||f||_D * eps. The leading term eps*||f||_D cannot be absorbed into eps*||A||*||f||_D unless ||A|| is bounded below by a fixed constant, but the paper only proves ||A||_{D->F} <= 1, and ||A|| can be arbitrarily small while nonzero (e.g. A scaled by a small constant). For such instances the achieved error is of order eps*||f||_D while the claimed bound is eps*||A||*||f||_D, so the stated probability guarantee is stronger than what is proved and fails in that regime.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the displayed bound to C*eps*||f||_D (equivalently choose delta_N with an extra 1/||A|| factor for nonzero A); this only changes constants, keeps the M-scaling structure and the advertised convergence order intact.
issues.overall_effect: The concluding probability statement of Theorem OC theorem (and its verbatim repetition in Theorem OC theorem noise) is unsupported; the order-of-convergence statements and the sample-complexity display are unaffected.
issues.title: Final accuracy display of Theorem OC theorem is stronger than what its proof establishes

issues.failure_explanation: For a 1-dimensional FEM basis of N hat functions on a fixed interval, the mesh size is h_N ~ 1/N (the paper's own Example FEM example gives N = O(h^{-d}), i.e. h^{-1} = Theta(N) for d = 1). Hence ||G_N^{-1}|| = Theta(h_N^{-1}) = Theta(N), not O(N^{1/2}); N^{1/2} is the d = 2 count. The example's claim is a concrete mathematical error, not a typo. Consequently its sample complexity M = O(eps^{-2-2/alpha} log(...)) is wrong: with ||G_N^{-1}|| = Theta(N) and kappa(G_N) bounded, equation (order of convergence) gives M = O(eps^{-2-4/alpha} log(.)), so the final cost O(MN) = O(eps^{-2-5/alpha} log(.)) differs from the dense-case cost O(eps^{-2-3/alpha}), and the stated conclusion 'This is equal to the cost in the previous example' is false.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we may apply Bernstein's inequality for the covariance defined in Corollary \ref{Bernstein Lemma} to \eqref{sum def}

issues.failure_explanation: By the paper's own definition of the perturbed Gram matrix, the summand is (Psi_N(x_m)+eta^m)(Psi_N(x_m)+eta^m)^dagger - G_N, whose expectation is G_N + E[eta(eta)^dagger], not G_N: the claim G_N = E[g g^dagger] in (gcmatdef) is false for any nondegenerate noise (for the advertised Gaussian noise, E[eta eta^dagger] = sigma^2 I). The summands S^G_m are therefore not centred, so Bernstein's inequality for the covariance (which requires mean zero) cannot be applied, and the inference 'tl{P}[norm(tl{G}-G) >= delta] <= ...' is unjustified. In fact G-tilde_{NM} -> G_N + E[eta eta^dagger] almost surely, so tl{A}_{NM}^top -> C_N(G_N+E[eta eta^dagger])^{-1} != (A_N^Psi)^top whenever C_N != 0; the proposition's guarantee ||tl{A}_{NM}-A_N|| <= c*delta for arbitrarily small delta (with probability >= p) is false for any fixed nondegenerate noise. (The proof also asserts 'the independence of g_m and c_m', but both contain the same eta^m.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must account for the deterministic bias: restate the bounds around the biased limits G_N + E[eta eta^dagger], C_N + E[xi eta^dagger] (i.e. convergence to C_N(G_N+E[eta eta^dagger])^{-1} rather than to A_N^Psi), or add new machinery (e.g. known noise covariance with an explicit debiasing step) and rebuild the centring/Bernstein argument; the advertised convergence of the noisy approximation to the true Galerkin operator cannot be retained under fixed nondegenerate noise.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition noise bound, Theorem OC theorem noise, the displayed rate (order of convergence noise), Example noise example 1, and the prose promises that accuracy is maintained under measurement error (abstract, Contribution 3, Section Noise section: 'We again show convergence of the approximations to the true dynamics in this case') are all unsupported; with fixed nondegenerate noise the noisy approximation does not converge to A_N at all.
issues.title: Noisy-data error bound is false: noisy empirical matrices concentrate around biased limits, so Bernstein's inequality is misapplied
issues.why_classification: Every resolution either adds a bias term that changes the guarantee type (no convergence of the noisy estimator to A_N, contradicting the advertised noisy-data regime of the abstract and Contribution 3) or requires new assumptions plus a re-engineered centring/estimation step; no local repair restores the stated guarantee, so the issue is serious.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: As a result, we obtain that $\tl{p}_N\geq 1-(2/e)^{\nicefrac N2}\approx 1 $.

issues.failure_explanation: The event is {|(eta^m, xi^m)|^2 <= gamma-tilde_N} with gamma-tilde_N = sigma^2 gamma_N = 2N sigma^2. Since eta and xi are independent N-dimensional Gaussians, sigma^{-2}|(eta,xi)|^2 ~ chi^2_{2N}, not chi^2_N; hence p-tilde_N = P[chi^2_{2N} <= 2N] which is about 1/2, not >= 1-(2/e)^{N/2} ~ 1. The example silently drops the degrees of freedom of the second noise vector (or treats the 2N-dimensional pair as N-dimensional), so its conclusion that the Gaussian noise 'effectively multipl[ies]' the error bound 'by a factor of 2' is wrong: at the chosen threshold only p-tilde_N ~ 0.5 is available, which in Proposition noise bound restricts p to below ~0.5.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute with the chi^2_{2N} distribution: either report the correct value p-tilde_N ~ 0.52 at gamma-tilde_N = sigma^2 gamma_N, or enlarge the threshold (e.g. gamma-tilde_N = c N sigma^2 with c large enough that the chi^2_{2N} tail is negligible) and redo the comparison with (order of convergence noise); a contained recomputation of the example.
issues.overall_effect: The example's quantitative claim about the size of the noise penalty in the theoretical bounds is wrong; it no longer supports the section's message that Gaussian noise has a small effect at this threshold.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption projection assumption is pointwise: for each fixed phi, ||P_{F_N} phi - phi|| -> 0. The proof applies it with phi = A f_{N_i}, where f_{N_i} varies with i and only ||f_{N_i}||_D = 1 is known. Strong convergence of projections gives no uniform control over bounded sets (e.g. coordinate projections on l^2 and phi_i = e_i give ||(Id-P_N)phi_i|| = 1 for all i), so the asserted norm convergence (Id - P_{F_{N_i}})A f_{N_i} -> 0 does not follow from the assumption. The defect is in the inference; the theorem itself remains true because only the scalar products against a fixed g are needed, and |<(Id-P_{N_i})A f_{N_i}, g>| <= ||A f_{N_i}||_F ||(Id-P_{N_i})g||_F <= ||f_{N_i}||_D ||(Id-P_{N_i})g||_F -> 0.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\big(\lambda_{N_i,M_i},f_{N_i,M_i}\big)$ be such a convergent sequence

By Corollary \ref{convergence data corollary}, for any $N \in \N$, there exists almost surely $M_N$ such that for all $M'_N \geq M_N$

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem asserts that for any sequence M'_{N_i} >= M_{N_i} the selected eigenpairs (lambda_{N_i M'_{N_i}}, f_{N_i M'_{N_i}}) converge to one limit (lambda, f). The proof only extracts a convergent subsequence of the diagonal pairs (lambda_{N_i,M_i}, f_{N_i,M_i}) and then works on that diagonal; nothing controls the selected eigenpairs at other sample sizes M' >= M_{N_i}, which are eigenpairs of different matrices wh-A_{N_i M'}. The claim is false for admissible selections: if the dictionary contains an A-invariant two-dimensional space carrying eigenvalues 1 and 2 at every N, and the eigenpair at (N,M) is selected to be the branch near 2 for odd M and near 1 for even M, then for any proposed (N_i, M_{N_i}) a parity-alternating choice M'_{N_i} >= M_{N_i} makes lambda_{N_i M'_{N_i}} oscillate. Additionally, the proof's justification of the second summand ('because of how (N_i,M'_{N_i}) was chosen') invokes the pointwise operator convergence of Theorem joint limit theorem at the moving argument f_{N_i,M'_{N_i}}, which that theorem (pointwise in a fixed argument) does not license; the step needs the operator-norm bound ||wh A_{N_i M'} - A_{N_i}|| < 1/(2N_i) instead. What the proof actually establishes is convergence along the extracted diagonal only.
